title: Writing With It
description: Use AI to write faster without producing writing that sounds like nobody. Covers the difference between drafting, editing and critique; how to keep your own voice instead of a smoothed-out default one; getting feedback that's actually specific; handling the messages you're dreading without inventing details or outsourcing tone; and naming the writing that's still worth doing yourself.

title: Research and Summarising
description: Use AI to get through material faster without losing accuracy. Covers the difference between summarising a document you actually provide and asking from the model's own memory, keeping the caveats a summary is tempted to drop, comparing sources without flattening real disagreement between them, what changes when a tool can search the live web, and how much of the original you actually need to read yourself to catch a wrong summary.

title: Learning With It
description: Use AI as a study partner without offloading the understanding. Covers getting explanations pitched at what you actually already know, asking to be quizzed instead of just told, recognising the specific feeling of a fluent explanation as unreliable evidence of real understanding, cross-checking a foundational explanation that might itself be wrong, and adapting active learning for a genuinely low-capacity day without it collapsing into passive reading.

title: Admin, Health and Life Logistics
description: Use AI for the paperwork and admin that chronic illness generates, safely. Covers drafting appeals and forms when you're too tired to write from scratch, preparing for an appointment without turning it into a diagnostic tool, parsing documents written to be hard to understand, what identifying and other people's data should never go into a consumer AI tool, and the real line between organizing medical information and diagnosing it.
